claims.head: Strength against strength
claims.body: The Stars are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Avalanche are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Stars’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.
claims.call: The Stars’ power play creates more than the league-average 7.6 expected goals per 60 against the Avalanche.
claims.nums: Dallas 2nd for the power play (9.4 expected goals per 60) · Colorado 2nd for the penalty kill

claims.head: Something has to give
claims.body: The Stars are near the top of the league for chance quality, but the Avalanche are the best at preventing dangerous shots. We’ll side with the Avalanche’s defense.
claims.call: The Avalanche keep the Stars’ chances less dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot).

claims.head: The Stars get in close, the Avalanche shoot from distance
claims.body: On shots from in close, Dallas is one of the league’s best, but Colorado is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Shots from in close tend to be more dangerous, so expect the Stars to do more of their damage around the net.

DAL.head: The Stars start a half-step behind
DAL.body: Even though Dallas has home-ice advantage, Colorado has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Stars can tip it if their penalty kill holds up.

COL.head: The Avalanche have a slight edge
COL.body: Even though Dallas has home-ice advantage, Colorado has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Stars can still swing it if their penalty kill holds up.

story.head: MacKinnon’s favorite opponent
paras: The Avalanche come in at 3-2-0, the Stars at 2-2-1. Two good teams meet.

It’s strength against strength: the Stars are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Avalanche are one of the best at the penalty kill. The Stars get in close, but the Avs mostly shoot from distance.

lean.DAL: Even though Dallas has home-ice advantage, Colorado has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Stars can tip it if their penalty kill holds up.
lean.COL: Even though Dallas has home-ice advantage, Colorado has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Stars can still swing it if their penalty kill holds up.

items.text: Nathan MacKinnon has a point in ten straight games against Dallas, and 18 points in his last eleven against them.
The Avalanche are newly without Cale Makar.
The Stars are newly without Wyatt Johnston, and have had to make do without Matt Duchene all season.
Mackenzie Blackwood has never won in Dallas: he is 0-3-1 there in his career.
